newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BURKS DOUBLE IN NINTH LIFTS ROCKIES PAST MARLINS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BURKS DOUBLE IN NINTH LIFTS ROCKIES PAST MARLINS.

text.p: Ellis Burks hit a two-out, two-run double off closer Robb Nen to cap a three-run ninth inning as the Colorado Rockies broke a 10-game losing streak in Florida with a 6-5 win over the Marlins Thursday.
Colorado's last win at Pro Player Stadium was on May 14, 1995.

Down 5-3 with two out in the ninth, the Rockies pulled within a run on Eric Young's RBI single to right field and completed their comeback with Burks's double into the left-centre field gap. Nen (4-2), who blew his fourth save opportunity of the season, suffered the loss.
"It's a big win off a tough pitcher in Robb Nen," said Burks. "The ninth inning showed we had some fight after what happened in the eighth."
The last-inning victory got Colorado starter Bobby Jones off the hook. The rookie gave up four runs and seven hits over six innings.
Colorado, trailing 4-0 in the sixth inning, got on the board with consecutive home runs by Larry Walker, Andres Galarraga and Dante Bichette off starter Alex Fernandez to pull within a run.
The Rockies last hit three straight homers on July 23, when Bichette, Galarraga and Vinny Castilla did it against Pete Harnisch and the Mets at Coors Field.
Darren Holmes (2-0) allowed a run in two innings of relief to earn the win and Steve Reed worked the ninth for his sixth save in nine opportunites.
"We haven't heard a lot of loud music in the clubhouse down in Florida lately," admitted Reed. "I didn't want to be the one walking off the field after blowing the lead. This is a huge win here."
Nen gave up three runs and three hits as the Marlins dropped two games in a row at home for just the second time this season.
The Florida closer was booed loudly after blowing the save. "I've got nothing to say to these fans," he said. "What do they want me to do, apologise to them?"
Kurt Abbott got his third career inside-the-park homer and the sixth in Marlins history in the third inning. Bobby Bonilla led off the fourth with his third homer of the season.

In San Francisco, Bill Mueller highlighted a three-run seventh with a two-run single and Shawn Estes (7-2) won his third straight start as the Giants rallied for a 4-2 victory over the Atlanta Braves.

Atlanta's John Smoltz (6-4) was cruising along with a two-hitter until the seventh. Smoltz struck out Barry Bonds, but three straight singles by Jeff Kent, J.T. Snow and Stan Javier drew San Francisco within 2-1.
A wild pitch put runners on second and third and Rick Wilkins walked to load the bases. Mueller then lined the first pitch from Smoltz into right field, scoring Snow and Javier for a 3-2 lead.
Bonds' sacrifice fly in the eighth scored Marvin Benard and increased the lead to 4-2.
Smoltz had his personal four-game winning streak snapped.

In Houston, Darryl Kile went seven innings for his fifth straight victory and helped himself with a two-run double during a six-run fourth as the Astros snapped a three-game losing streak, 10-6 over the slumping San Diego Padres.

Kile (6-2) improved to 5-0 with a 1.20 ERA in May. He allowed five runs and eight hits with three walks and nine strikeouts. In his previous five starts, he had surrendered just two runs and 23 hits over 38 innings.
Steve Finley and Ken Caminiti each drove in two runs for San Diego, which has allowed 46 runs during a five-game losing streak.
Fernando Valenzuela (2-7) suffered his sixth loss in seven decisions.
In Chicago, Steve Trachsel pitched eight strong innings and Brant Brown's RBI double off reliever Stan Belinda (0-1) in the eighth inning lifted the Cubs to a 2-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds.

Trachsel (3-4) allowed one run and three hits. Trachsel has allowed just six earned runs in 27 2/3 innings (1.95 ERA) over his last four starts. He also knocked in the Cubs' first runs with a groundout in the fifth scoring Scott Servais.
Joe Oliver homered for Cincinnati's lone run.
In St Louis, Matt Morris allowed one run over eight innings and Gary Gaetti's home run snapped a tie in the fourth inning as the Cardinals beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 4-2.

Morris (2-3) allowed eight hits and struck out seven without walking a batter in his 10th major-league start. Dennis Eckersley earned his 10th save, allowing one run and two hits with a strikeout in the ninth inning.
It was the fourth win in five games for the Cardinals.
Pedro Astacio (3-4) took the loss.
